# 04 `graph` is a spelling of `flowchart`

## Outcome

`graph TB`, `graph LR` and the rest parse exactly as `flowchart TB` does. The word is an alias,
and nothing downstream learns there are two spellings.

## Why this ticket exists

`graph` is Mermaid's original keyword and still the one most documents in the wild open with.
Siren rejects it outright, which means a large share of real Mermaid flowcharts fail on line one.

This is board 1's `TD` → `TB` rule again, at the other end of the same header: normalize the
authored spelling at the parser, keep one vocabulary downstream. The repo has done it three times
since (`cssClass` → `apply`, a `linkStyle` index → an edge id, `color` → `fill`), and
`parser/parseDirection.ts` is where that pattern lives.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `graph TB`, `graph BT`, `graph LR`, `graph RL` and `graph TD` all parse, with `TD`
      normalizing to `TB` exactly as it does after `flowchart`.
- [x] Nothing downstream can tell which word the author wrote. `FlowchartDocument` gains no field
      for it — check `parseDirection.ts` for how `TD` is handled and follow it. If a diagnostic
      needs to quote the author's word, say so in your report rather than adding a field silently;
      note that board 3 hit exactly this and added `StyleDecl.authoredAs` for a *stated* reason.
- [x] The unrecognized-header diagnostic names `graph` among the accepted spellings, in both
      `parseFlowchart` and `parseSiren`. `listAcceptedHeaders` already exists for this — use it
      rather than writing a second list, since the whole point of that helper is that the
      dispatcher and the parser cannot name different sets.
- [x] `CONTEXT.md`'s **Diagram kind** entry names the alias, the way it already names `TD`.
- [x] The corpus's two `graph` entries move to `supported`, each with an `assert` that checks the
      parsed direction — not merely that it rendered. `rejected` down two.

## Status

Done (2026-09-06), commit ce9c8b9. 3 slices, all red-green. 689 core tests / 29 board, tsc clean
both. Ratchets: rejected 39 → **37**, silently-wrong untouched at **2**.

No field records the authored keyword: the `authoredAs` bar was not met, because no diagnostic
quotes the keyword — they quote the offending line verbatim. The test proves it by comparing the
two ParseResults for equality, so a leak would fail rather than pass unnoticed.

## Test seam

`parseSiren` and `parseFlowchart` through the source string; the behavior is in the header text,
so a hand-built document cannot catch a regex that still rejects the word.
